Belligerent

buh-LIJ-ur-unt -- Latin bellum ('war') plus gerere ('to wage'): someone who carries a war around with them. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Belligerent is eager to be hostile or aggressive.

The belligerent customer demanded to see a manager before anyone had even spoken to him.

Worked Example

A player who has already been warned twice bumps the umpire's shoulder, kicks dirt across the plate, and dares him to say another word.

Actively looking for a fight is exactly what belligerent describes. Unlike 'angry,' which can stay quiet inside a person, belligerent anger reaches outward and picks at other people.

How Belligerent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

quarrelsome

quarrelsome: quick to start arguments

combative

combative: ready and eager to fight

aggressive

aggressive: forceful and threatening toward others

Antonyms

peaceable

peaceable: inclined to avoid conflict

friendly

friendly: warm and welcoming toward others

How Strong Is It? — quarrelsome → combative → belligerent

quarrelsome vs. belligerent

quarrelsome vs. belligerent: Quarrelsome is the milder word -- a quarrelsome person bickers, while a belligerent one looks ready to take the argument outside.

combative vs. belligerent

combative vs. belligerent: Combative is belligerent at full strength: belligerent describes someone spoiling for conflict, while combative suggests they treat every conversation as a fight already underway.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — belli-

root — belli-: war (Latin (bellum))

root — -ger-

root — -ger-: to carry on, to wage (Latin (gerere))

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: adjective-forming: doing the action (Latin (-entem))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin belligerare meant 'to wage war,' from bellum ('war') and gerere ('to carry on') -- a belligerent person is waging a small private war on everyone nearby, from the same bellum root that gives us rebellion.

Use the root in a new word: rebellion

Use the root in a new word: rebellion: The rebellion began with farmers refusing to hand over the harvest tax.

Root Check

Word Choice

Belligerent describes people and their behavior -- a belligerent tone, a belligerent drunk. As a noun it has a formal military meaning too: the belligerents in a conflict are the nations actually fighting it.
